root.title: Canonical problem
root.currentStateSummary: A finite-block code-induced dependence-balance condition and compatible rate inequalities are established. An exact finite entropic witness also shows that the specified entropy-only and finite copy-lemma relaxation cannot improve the classical UV value. These results constrain converse strategies but do not change the certified capacity frontier or numerical upper bound.
root.localResidualSummary: Determine the BSSC sum capacity or strengthen its certified converse, including through a valid support reduction, globally certified optimization, exact binary-posterior consistency constraints, or direct multiletter code inequalities beyond the obstructed entropy/copy relaxation.

prog-code-induced-converse.title: Code-induced BSSC converse structure
prog-code-induced-converse.objective: Convert structural constraints inherited from reliable private-message codes into rigorous, optimizable BSSC converse bounds and identify refinements capable of improving the certified bound.
prog-code-induced-converse.currentStateSummary: Every deterministic finite-block code induces an asymptotically exact dependence-balance relation, a fixed-coordinate encoder law, and four compatible rate inequalities. A finite entropic counterfeit proves that the specified universal entropy-inequality and finite copy-lemma refinement route cannot beat the classical UV value. The remaining viable directions require support reduction or genuinely channel-specific consistency information.
prog-code-induced-converse.localResidualSummary: Prove a support or compactness reduction preserving the induced law and rate rows, certify any resulting global optimization, or derive exact jointly consistent binary-BSSC posterior constraints or direct multiletter inequalities that exclude the entropic counterfeit and strengthen the converse.

prog-uv-scalar-product-additivity.title: UV scalar product additivity and symmetry
prog-uv-scalar-product-additivity.objective: Determine the tensorization and blocking behavior of separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar functionals, including symmetry conditions that identify their branchwise and averaged forms.
prog-uv-scalar-product-additivity.currentStateSummary: The averaged separately relaxed UV scalar is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, even with correlated product-channel inputs and joint envelope auxiliaries. Receiver-skew symmetry equates the branchwise and averaged scalars and is preserved by finite products. Consequently, every finite power of the half-skew BSSC has normalized value 2h2(1/4)-5/4, which is weaker than the certified capacity upper bound and does not change the capacity frontier.
prog-uv-scalar-product-additivity.localResidualSummary: Determine whether any stronger coupled UV formulation, complete UV region, other weighted scalarization, nested auxiliary construction, or full Theorem-9 system tensorizes or can yield a sharper BSSC converse; the established theorem does not cover those objectives.

ir-code-induced-balance-entropy-nogo.title: Code-induced dependence balance and entropy/copy no-go theorem
scopeQualifications: No achievability result, capacity formula, global converse optimum, or improvement over the existing certified BSSC upper bound follows.
The alphabets of U, V, and W may grow with blocklength, so the condition is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region or a certified numerical capacity bound.
The entropic witness is not generated by a binary BSSC: its X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components, and exact binary-posterior consistency excludes it.

The finite-block necessary condition applies to deterministic private-message codes on finite-alphabet memoryless two-receiver broadcast channels and hence to the BSSC; reliable bounded-rate sequences make its dependence-balance defect vanish.

The no-go theorem concerns only the precisely stated entropy/copy relaxation at uniform input; it does not preclude binary-BSSC posterior constraints, jointly consistent channel-specific refinements, or direct code inequalities.

proofs: Conditioning on (A,B,T) fixes the current input, while channel memorylessness separates the current output pair from the past/future state W. Chain rules and conditioned Csiszar sum identities give the four rate rows without an unproved sign assumption.

Define Di=I(A;B|Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n). Each balance summand is Di-D_{i-1}, giving the exact telescope. Nonnegativity and separate Fano bounds control the two endpoints and yield the absolute defect bound after time sharing.

Every standard copy step is realizable by conditional resampling of the finite witness, preserving its original marginal and objective; universal finite-variable information inequalities also hold because the witness is genuinely entropic.

For the no-go theorem, a calculus argument gives the sharp scalar BSSC support value r=h2(1/4)-3/4. An explicit tuple construction from independent binary components realizes all required entropy, structural, dependence-balance, conditional BEC, and support constraints and attains both objective branches exactly.
methods: Exact affine-in-h component-entropy construction and set-union/intersection evaluation of entropies and conditional mutual informations.
Finite-block telescoping, separate Fano endpoint control, time sharing with the encoder-coordinate map retained, and conditioned Csiszar identities.
computations: The exact standard-library checker verify_exact_witness.py (SHA-256 0be3d1bf7dfc02f22cc55cd52fafcb7e9290cfb32db7d4a103a570deefb0f32b) verifies component positivity, the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, both zero dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both support rows, and both objective branches without floating-point arithmetic.
tools: Python 3 standard-library symbolic checker representing every entropy as a rational affine expression in h=h2(1/4) and evaluating tuple variables through independent-component set operations.

ir-uv-product-branchwise-additivity.title: Exact UV product and receiver-skew branchwise additivity
ir-uv-product-branchwise-additivity.statement: For a finite-alphabet DMBC W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let C denote the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p (A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg(W1×W2)=B_avg(W1)+B_avg(W2) for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs, including correlated product-channel priors and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges the receivers, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products preserve this symmetry, so both functionals are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of receiver-skew-symmetric channels. For the half-skew BSSC P, the invariant binary prior is fair and, using the accepted sharp BSSC posterior support, B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h2(1/4)-5/4) for every finite n≥1, with normalized value 0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use.
scopeQualifications: Branchwise equality is established under receiver-skew symmetry and is not claimed for nonsymmetric channels or other weighted UV scalarizations.
No achievability result or capacity formula follows.

The half-skew BSSC value is a valid non-frontier converse value. It exceeds the certified full-Theorem-9 upper bound 0.369296945969202842443 and therefore changes neither endpoint of the governed capacity interval.

The theorem concerns the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate rows and their averaged or pointwise-minimum scalarizations; it does not establish tensorization of the complete UV rate region or simultaneous attainment by a common joint (U,V) law.
The theorem does not tensorize the simplified GK functional, nested auxiliary-receiver constructions, or the full Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem-9 constraint system.

proofs: For a product DMBC and an arbitrary auxiliary A, a forward/reverse chain-rule expansion gives an exact cancellation of the cross co-information terms at coefficient one. The conditioned variables remaining in the two summands are valid one-factor auxiliaries, yielding factorwise upper bounds for both concave envelopes even under correlated inputs.

For the half-skew BSSC, the sharp posterior-support inequality and its reflected form identify the fair-prior envelope contact. The source mixture supported at posterior parameters 0 and 4/5 attains the contact, giving the exact one-letter value 2h2(1/4)-5/4.

Mutual-information subadditivity and the envelope inequalities give the product upper bound for B_avg. Product priors together with independent near-optimal posterior decompositions give the reverse inequality and hence exact additivity.

The coordinatewise receiver-skew involution makes every finite product receiver-skew-symmetric. Combining symmetry equality with averaged-functional additivity proves finite-product additivity of both scalar functionals.

Under the receiver-skew involution S, t(Sp)=-t(p), the envelope decompositions are carried bijectively to one another, and A_W(Sp)=D_W(p). Concavity at the invariant symmetrization (p+Sp)/2 proves B_br≥B_avg, while min(a,d)≤(a+d)/2 proves the reverse inequality.
methods: Analytic proofs are retained in source-artifacts/upper-uv-additivity/FULL.md (SHA-256 69a33f9fc84a5dbabbad6bdf53b34e722238c6a6b3f625d49e00f599e942b94a) and source-artifacts/frontier-uv-branchwise/FULL.md (SHA-256 64ddb2c3d0c375bbca746842e21689f11883d989d56a0f0028ceaf216715e623).
Dependency-ordered specialization using the sharp BSSC posterior support represented by ir-code-induced-balance-entropy-nogo.

Exact chain-rule factorization for product broadcast channels, upper-concave-envelope decomposition, mutual-information subadditivity, product posterior mixtures, involutive receiver-exchange covariance, and concavity-based symmetrization.
computations: A 90-digit Decimal audit checks the BSSC envelope contact, fair-prior barycenter, receiver-skew matrices, and exact-form numerical evaluation.
The BSSC specialization evaluates exactly to 2h2(1/4)-5/4=0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use; finite powers multiply this value by the blocklength.
The normalized UV value 0.3725562489182657… is numerically larger, and hence weaker as an upper bound, than the certified full-Theorem-9 value 0.369296945969202842443.
tools: Python 3 hostile-case audit verify_uv_hostile_cases.py (SHA-256 ffa2b5d66670f0fd03338e73f8ecc5400bf23b162a92fa327f363c7bb1aac6c0) checks deterministic and zero-probability channels, correlated and degenerate inputs, receiver-skew matrices, and the high-precision BSSC specialization.

Python 3 standard-library audit source-artifacts/upper-uv-additivity/verify_uv_factorization.py (SHA-256 bdd966d11f1914425ed4932b459c83508a6a61a73131f4f2a184204ad0c4153e) checks the product chain identities, conditional Markov relations, mutual-information subadditivity, product mixtures, and BSSC contact value.
